incident: Users experienced failures when attempting to download crates from crates.io, resulting in broken package retrieval.
logs:
[12:34:56] ERROR: Failed to generate download URL for crate 'serde' version '1.0.0'
[12:35:01] WARN: Download request for crate 'tokio' returned 404
[12:35:05] ERROR: URL generation service returned invalid path
[12:35:10] INFO: Retrying download for crate 'rand' after URL error
metrics: Error rate for crate downloads spiked from 0.1% to 85%, average download latency increased by 300ms
deployments: Deployment of URL generation service update at 12:30 UTC
expected_root_cause: crates.io download breakage from deployment bug in URL generation

incident: All Stack Exchange sites experienced an outage lasting approximately 6 minutes due to connectivity issues between load balancers and web servers.
logs:
[19:26:15] ERROR: Connection to IIS web server timed out
[19:27:00] WARN: HAProxy unable to complete connection, retrying
[19:27:30] INFO: Reverting recent firewall configuration change
[19:32:00] INFO: Connection restored, traffic flowing normally
metrics: Increased connection timeouts to IIS web servers; spike in failed TCP handshakes; overall site availability dropped to 0%
deployments: Change to iptables firewall configuration pushed to Git at 19:01
expected_root_cause: Incorrect firewall configuration on HAProxy load balancers blocked response traffic, causing the outage.

incident: Cloudflare experienced DNS resolution failures affecting 1.1.1.1 and related services from 07:00 to 11:00 UTC on October 4, 2023.
logs:
[07:01:15] ERROR: Failed to parse DNS root zone record ZONEMD
[07:05:42] WARN: Serving stale root zone data due to parse failure
[08:30:10] ERROR: DNS query returned SERVFAIL for valid requests
[10:59:59] INFO: Root zone parsing issue resolved, normal service resuming
metrics: DNS SERVFAIL error rate spiked from 0% to 15% during incident; query latency increased by 20%; successful resolution rate dropped by 30%
expected_root_cause: Cloudflare DNS resolution failures were caused by an internal software error parsing the new ZONEMD record in the root zone, not a recent deployment.
